calibration.historical_selection_scope: The three historical baselines use different reblocking/frequency calibration families. This review does not assert a joint best-of-nine daily bound from selection_methods16/calibration_segments2.
calibration.method_scope: Six separate score alternatives,not a six-model likelihood mixture. Every model mixes its complete timing×CFO bank. All six new models share the same reblock4 residual calibration for each capture.
calibration.null_scope: Stationary proper-complex white Gaussian H0 and a genuinely predeclared finite family; no adaptive stopping,unbounded continued tuning,wrong-key or correct-bit guarantee.

conclusion: The screen recovers selected short-window failures but does not beat existing whole-observation reception on these captures. The random25 miss persists. No new receiver algorithm or default is justified by this five-capture screen.
limitations: Cases were chosen after failures; the six choices are fixed for this small screen,not prospective independent qualification.
Reblocking4 changes the retained projection and noise-residual family as well as coefficient center spacing. Comparing new0.5/2/4s models with old62.5ms windows is not a pure duration ablation.
B=0.2Hz is a receiver Gaussian-coefficient width,not a change to physical ray separation or added modulation. No physical samples/noise/seeds were regenerated.
All six new models include the public CFO bank; historical window and zero-CFO global did not. Use historical global-frequency as the acquisition-matched comparison.
One null and two wrong-key captures,each reused six times,do not become18 independent controls.
Report array bounds are not observed peak RSS. No GPU acceleration or ordinary receiver integration is demonstrated.
